### 1.1-1.3 Problem Analysis

The issue is with **date localization** in the mkdocs-git-revision-date-localized-plugin. When a user sets a locale (like `fr` for French) in their mkdocs configuration, the dates should be displayed in that locale's language, but they're currently showing in English regardless of the locale setting.

### 1.4 Steps to Reproduce
1. Set `locale: fr` in mkdocs configuration file
2. Serve the site using `mkdocs serve -f tests/basic_setup/mkdocs_locale.yml`
3. Observe that dates appear in English instead of French

### 1.5 Technical Details
- **File affected**: `mkdocs_git_revision_date_localized_plugin/util.py`
- **Line**: 81
- **Method**: `_date_formats`
- **Issue**: The `locale` parameter is not being passed to the `_date_formats` method
- **Suggested fix**: Pass the inherited `locale` parameter

     9	# mkdocs-git-revision-date-localized-plugin
    10	
    11	[MkDocs](https://www.mkdocs.org/) plugin that enables displaying the date of the last git modification of a page. The plugin uses [babel](https://github.com/python-babel/babel/tree/master/babel) and [timeago.js](https://github.com/hustcc/timeago.js) to provide different localized date formats. Initial fork from [mkdocs-git-revision-date-plugin](https://github.com/zhaoterryy/mkdocs-git-revision-date-plugin).
    12	
    13	![example](https://github.com/timvink/mkdocs-git-revision-date-localized-plugin/raw/master/example.png)
    14	
    15	(*Example when used together with [mkdocs-material](https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material) theme*)
    16	
    17	## Setup
    18	
    19	Install the plugin using `pip` with the following command:
    20	
    21	```bash
    22	pip install mkdocs-git-revision-date-localized-plugin
    23	```
    24	
    25	Next, add the following lines to your `mkdocs.yml`:
    26	
    27	```yaml
    28	plugins:
    29	  - search
    30	  - git-revision-date-localized
    31	```
    32	
    33	> If you have no `plugins` entry in your config file yet, you'll likely also want to add the `search` plugin. MkDocs enables it by default if there is no `plugins` entry set.
    34	
    35	### When using CI runners
    36	
    37	The plugin needs access to the last commit that touched a file to be able to retrieve the date. If you build your docs using CI then you might need to change the default settings:
    38	
    39	- github actions: set `fetch_depth` to `0` ([docs](https://github.com/actions/checkout))
    40	- gitlab runners: set `GIT_DEPTH` to `1000` ([docs](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/project/pipelines/settings.html#git-shallow-clone))
    41	
    42	----
    43	
    44	## Usage
    45	
    46	### In supported themes
    47	
    48	- [mkdocs-material](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/) offers support for this plugin, see [setup instructions](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/plugins/revision-date/)
    49	
    50	### In theme templates
    51	
    52	In templates you can use `page.meta.git_revision_date_localized`:
    53	
    54	```django hljs
    55	{% if page.meta.git_revision_date_localized %}
    56	  Last update: {{ page.meta.git_revision_date_localized }}
    57	{% endif %}
    58	```
    59	
    60	### In markdown pages
    61	
    62	In your markdown files you can use `{{ git_revision_date_localized }}`:
    63	
    64	```django hljs
    65	Last update: {{ git_revision_date_localized }}
    66	```
    67	
    68	## Options
    69	
    70	### `type`
    71	
    72	To change the date format, set the `type` parameter to one of `date`, `datetime`, `iso_date`, `iso_datetime` or `timeago`. Default is `date`. Example outputs:
    73	
    74	```bash
    75	28 November, 2019           # type: date
    76	28 November, 2019 13:57:28  # type: datetime
    77	2019-11-28                  # type: iso_date
    78	2019-11-28 13:57:26         # type: iso_datetime
    79	20 hours ago                # type: timeago
    80	```
    81	
    82	### `locale`
    83	
    84	Specify a two letter [ISO639](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes) language code to display dates in your preferred language.
    85	
    86	- When used in combination with `type: date` or `type: datetime`, translation is done using [babel](https://github.com/python-babel/babel) which supports [these locales](http://www.unicode.org/cldr/charts/latest/supplemental/territory_language_information.html)
    87	- When used in combination with `type: timeago` then [timeago.js](https://github.com/hustcc/timeago.js) is added to your website, which supports [these locales](https://github.com/hustcc/timeago.js/tree/master/src/lang). If you specify a locale not supported by timeago.js, the fallback is English (`en`)
    88	- When not set, this plugin will look for `locale` or `language` options set in your theme. If also not set, the fallback is English (`en`)
    89	
    90	### `fallback_to_build_date`
    91	
    92	If you need to ignore the Git exceptions during `git log` operations, set this option to `true` (default is `false`).
    93	
    94	In addition, if you need to completely ignore if Git is reachable or installed, you should set the environment variable ["GIT_PYTHON_REFRESH"] to `quiet`.
    95	
    96	----
    97	
    98	### Example
    99	
   100	Example with all options:
   101	
   102	```yaml
   103	# mkdocs.yml
   104	plugins:
   105	  - git-revision-date-localized:
   106	    locale: en
   107	    type: timeago
   108	    fallback_to_build_date: true
   109	```
   110	
   111	Result:
   112	
   113	```txt
   114	20 hours ago
   115	```
